what: check_pr_landing resolves a branch's declaration by BRANCH SLUG (.github/pr-landing/<slug>.json), so a branch RE-CUT from main after its PR merged still carries that merged PR's declaration -- and if the merged PR was a Tier-2 `hold`, R10 refuses any follow-up arming on the same slug. The harness's own guidance says to re-cut the designated branch KEEPING ITS NAME after a merge, so this is reachable from following the documented path, not from doing something unusual. !! THE HAZARD IS THE CHEAPEST FIX, NOT THE REFUSAL: the one-file way past R10 is to rewrite the merged PR's declaration to `tier: 1` / `landing: self`, which satisfies the guard by DESTROYING the record of why that PR was held -- on the one file whose entire job is carrying an attributable landing claim, and which .github/pr-landing/README.md describes as the record a reviewer reads. A guard whose cheapest satisfaction is falsifying the record it protects is the same shape this repo already names for new-table-wiring-guard's presence-only marker ('cheaper to lie to than to satisfy').
